mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over two months signals increased demand for housing and related goods, which can boost economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a slowdown in economic activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over three months signals strong consumer demand, which can boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when the signal is active.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals an economic downturn, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth is negative for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.
